paper_title: Particle dispersion in the classical vector dark matter background
notes: Dashed green (delta m_e^earth) line in Fig. 6 (DPbounds.pdf), the paper's new dark-photon bound from the electron mass measurement, Eq. (35): g_e < 3.3e-12 (m/1e-20 eV) at local DM density 0.3 GeV/cm^3, converted to kinetic mixing via eps = g_e/e giving eps < 1.1e-11 (m/1e-20 eV). Vector extraction of the figure confirms this exactly (log-log slope 1.000, eps=1.10e-11 at 1e-20 eV); points span the line's extent within the figure frame (1e-20 to 3e-11 eV, where it exits the plot top). The paper also draws a stronger dashed black 'Z' line from electroweak-precision wavefunction-normalization arguments, Eq. (39): eps < 2.2e-38 (m/1e-20 eV)^2 (verified in the figure, slope 2.000, spanning ~3e-13 to 2e-2 eV within the frame); I report the delta m_e dispersion bound as the main result since the abstract and conclusions present the dispersion/refraction bound as the headline dark-photon constraint, with the Z bound framed as a generic VDM normalization constraint. Confidence level not stated explicitly; density quoted at 2-sigma. Assumes vector field is all of the local DM.
